pk/math.text: Demonstrate knowledge of numbers, numerals, and quantity.
Recite numbers from 1 to 20.
Count backward from 5 to 1.
Give the next number name in the number series up to 10.
Recognize mistakes in others’ counting and self-correct own counting.
Identify and use numbers related to order or position from first to fifth.
Count up to 10 objects saying the number name in the correct order and pairing each object with one and only one number name.
Count using one-to-one correspondence and answer “How many?” questions for a group of up to 10 objects arranged in a straight line.
Instantly recognize and name the number of objects in a set up to five.
Manipulate a set of objects to count out a specified or target number of up to 10 objects.
Correctly identify the remaining number of objects in a set of up to four objects after one object is added or taken away.
Compare two or more sets of up to 10 objects and accurately identify which sets are equal and which have more or fewer objects.
Recognize and read some of the numerals between 0 and 10.
Match the number of objects in a set to the correct numeral between 1 and 5.
Write, draw, or create objects to represent the numerals between 0 and 5.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and create patterns and early mathematical problem-solving skills.
Sort objects by attributes such as size and shape.
Recognize, replicate, and extend simple repeating patterns.
Create own simple pattern and identify the core unit of the repeating pattern.
Solve simple addition and subtraction problems (where the answer is five or less), using objects to represent the problem.
Demonstrate the ability to measure and compare by size and volume.
Compare or order up to five objects based on their measurable attributes, such as height or weight.
Use comparative language to describe the length, size, or weight of two or more objects (e.g., shortest, heavier, biggest).
Measure the length of an object using another object or group of objects.
Analyze and compare common shapes and use knowledge of position in space.
Identify basic shapes such as circles, triangles, squares, and rectangles regardless of size or orientation.
Name, describe, and compare shapes in terms of length of sides, number of sides, and number of angles.
Identify basic 2D and 3D shapes in the environment.
Create and build shapes from components.
Select, combine, rotate, and flip shapes to match an example.
Understand and use language related to directionality and the position of objects.

pk/language.text: Demonstrate the ability to attend to and understand communication from others.
Use verbal and nonverbal signals to acknowledge communication from others.
Show ongoing connection to a conversation, group discussion, or presentation.
Recall and follow two- and three-step directions.
Show understanding of books read aloud, stories, or explanations on a topic.
Listen with increasing attention span to gain new knowledge.
Demonstrate the ability to express themselves verbally or nonverbally.
Communicate to express self in detailed ways.
Communicate in complete sentences using at least three words.
Follow conventions of conversation most of the time.
Share ideas and information from personal and group experiences.
Communicate to express needs and clarify a word or statement when misunderstood.
Use a variety of vocabulary words during play and other activities.
Use vocabulary words with increasing specificity and variety to describe feelings, experiences, observations, and ideas.
Use context to determine the meaning of unknown words.
Use a wide variety of words for many purposes.
Use words that describe a category of objects that go together.
Identify common opposite words.
Use words with similar meaning to describe an object, emotion, or action.
Discuss and use new vocabulary words learned from stories, books, and/or other early literacy activities.
Demonstrate knowledge of the alphabet and how letters are used in the reading process.
Identify the names of letters in own name and produce the sound of the first letter in own name.
Identify and name most letters in their uppercase form and some letters in their lowercase form.
Name and produce the letter sound for several letters.
Demonstrate knowledge of how print and books are read.
Recognize that print carries a message and information.
Recognize environmental print and symbols.
Indicate that groups of letters form a word.
Identify book parts and features, such as the front, back, title, and/or author.
Demonstrate knowledge gained from stories, books, and other early literacy activities.
Ask questions or make comments related to the details of a story.
Retell a story, putting at least two events in the appropriate sequence.
Predict what might happen next in a story.
Recall information and answer questions related to an event, text, or pictures related to self and the world around them.
Use pictures to gain meaning and follow a simple pictorial direction.
Demonstrate the use of written letters and symbols to communicate.
Draw to express ideas, thoughts, or interests.
Experiment with writing tools and materials for variety of purposes.
Recreate basic shapes that form letters or draw the shapes while looking at a model.
Write for a variety of purposes using increasingly sophisticated marks.
Use letter-like approximation to print name.
Share ideas, information from experiences, and opinions for class writing.
Dictate words, phrases, or sentences to an adult who writes them down.
Demonstrate knowledge of sounds within spoken language
Repeat rhyming words.
Identify beginning sounds of some spoken words with which they are familiar.
Identify two or more spoken words that share the same initial sound.
Identify multiple parts of short words and long words.

pk/science.text: Demonstrate the ability to use senses and tools to explore, make observations, and make predictions.
Use smell, touch, sight, sound, and taste to make observations.
Use tools to observe and describe objects, the environment, and processes.
Use observations and information to notice patterns, create groups based on similarities/ differences observed, and/ or make predictions.
Make predictions using prior knowledge and experience.
Demonstrate the ability to use information gathered in different ways to conduct investigations.
Show curiosity and ask questions about things they are interested in that can be answered through an investigation.
Describe some of the steps and/or materials needed for an investigation or experiment.
Conduct simple investigations and gather information through observations to see what happens.
Demonstrate the ability to describe, analyze, and draw conclusions about the outcome of an investigation.
Analyze observations from an investigation to develop an explanation or conclusion.
Describe possible cause and effect relationships from observation or prior knowledge.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate about observations, investigations, and outcomes.
Create pictures, diagrams, or 3D models to represent plans for an investigation.
Illustrate or describe observations, results, and conclusions or explanations from an investigation or science-related activities.
Use scientific content words during scientific inquiry and investigation.
Use adjectives and scientific words to describe objects, materials, organisms, events, and processes.

Demonstrate a basic awareness of self as an individual, within the context of a group and community.
Identify and describe characteristics of self that are unique from others.
Identify self as a member of a family.
Share information about their family practices, customs, and culture.
Identify and describe family traditions and daily rituals that are important to their family.
Demonstrate a basic understanding of roles, rights, and responsibilities in their classroom and home.
Identify self as member of a classroom or community.
Identify classroom teachers/ practitioners and peers by name.
Recognize and resolve conflicts with peers in an age-appropriate manner.
Show awareness of and follow group routines and rules.
Participate in group decision-making.
Work together to complete simple tasks with peers.
Identify and describe the roles of different community helpers.
Demonstrate knowledge of the relationship between people and places.
Use spatial words to identify direction and location.
Identify and describe their classroom, home, or community.
Identify differences and similarities between home and school.
Recognize that peers live in different places within the community.
Recognize and identify some tools and resources used to describe features of places.
Identify and describe environmental and geographical features of the area where they live.
Participate in taking care of the world around them.
Demonstrate the ability to differentiate between the concepts of past, present, and future, and recognize that people and things change over time
Describe a sequence of events.
Recognize a change in a sequence of events.
Recognize changes that take place over time.
Describe events that happened in the immediate past or are planned for the near future.
Demonstrate an awareness of basic economic concepts.
Recognize that resources can be limited.
Recognize that people may want something, which is different from something they need.
Decide between at least two choices involving resources in the classroom or at home.
Recognize that people use money to buy things they want and need.
Demonstrate curiosity and initiative .
Ask questions and seek new information related to a variety of topics, ideas, and activities.
Seek out and explore unfamiliar objects and activities.
Initiate activities or tasks.
Make choices and communicate their choice to adults and other children.
Demonstrate willingness to take risks and use flexibility in thinking and actions.
Try or join in new activities and experiences, even if they are perceived as challenging.
Use a variety of approaches and strategies to complete tasks and solve problems.
Try different strategies to resolve conflict or other problems in working with other children.
Recognize and attempt to correct mistakes.
Use rules from one situation as a guide for behavior in a different situation.
Delay gratification to complete a larger task.
Manage transition between activities without getting frustrated.
Demonstrate the ability to focus attention and persist in an activity.
Maintain focus on activities for developmentally appropriate periods of time.
Persist in tasks and re-engage in an activity after an interruption.
Express satisfaction when accomplishing a task and achieving a goal.
Continue with a task or activity even when it is challenging or frustrating.
Demonstrate imagination and engage in different types of play
Use imagination in social and pretend play.
Give and follow directions from peers during social play.
Communicate in a variety of ways when playing with others.
Use what was learned in other disciplines in pretend play.
Act out or create a new role based on life experiences, including collaboration with peers in related roles.
Use materials or objects to represent something else during play or when acting out stories.
Differentiate between pretend and real.
